newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGC says develops low-cost refinery.
newsitem.headline: JGC says develops low-cost refinery.

text.p: JGC Corp, a leading engineering company, said on Tuesday it had developed a low-cost oil refinery which could desulphurise various oil products at the same time, instead of using separate desulphurising units.
The technology is suited for small and medium-sized refineries with capacities of about 20,000 to 50,000 barrels per day, a JGC spokesman said.
A conventional refinery needs about five desulphurisers, one for each oil product, such as naphtha and kerosene, produced from the crude distillation unit.
JGC said the new refinery would cost about 30 billion yen.
Construction costs had been cut by simplifying the structure of the crude distillation unit as well as rationalising the desulphurising process, the spokesman said.
It takes two years to construct the refinery, compared with the usual three, he said.
Sales are targeted at emerging countries where there is a need to quickly construct oil refineries due to surging oil product demand, he said.
